title: New Lagos Rising Again
premise: Felix Thackeray discovers that the 'backups' in his cargo hold are not dormant data but sleeping copies of colonists harvested by the orbital authority of New Lagos, and that the children's shared dream is the backups' consciousness leaking through the station's relay network. When the authority begins purging the hold to bury the evidence, Felix, disgraced medic Ada Okonkwo, and the dream-touched girl Ngozi must steal his own ship and run for the dead-space relay where the backups can broadcast their testimony to every colony at once. The climax comes at the relay, where Felix must merge a fragment of his own mind with the network to complete the broadcast, sacrificing the version of himself he trusts most. The signal goes out, the authority falls, and Felix returns to New Lagos changed—no longer invisible, and no longer entirely sure which of him survived.
about_author: Silas Ravensworth is the pen name of a former merchant-marine radio operator who spent a decade writing stories in shipping containers between ports. New Lagos Rising Again is the third novel in a loosely connected series about people who live in the gaps that power leaves unwatched.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbits; Felix avoids the hold where the 'backups' sleep, a superstition he's kept for five years. A minor navigation anomaly near the relay corridor unsettles him. Emotional beat: quiet dread, the sense that his invisibility is fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. On New Lagos colony, twelve children describe an identical dream: a dark room, warm lights, a voice counting. Their teacher reports it; an authority assessor arrives within hours, faster than any bureaucracy should move. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into the first taste of surveillance.

chapters.title: Manifest Discrepancies
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Docking at New Lagos, Felix is ordered to surrender his hold manifest. He notices his cargo codes have been altered in transit. Ada Okonkwo, a medic stripped of license for asking about the backups, warns him what happens to ships that ask questions. Emotional beat: paranoia becoming evidence.

chapters.title: What the Assessor Knows
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada is detained and questioned about the children's dreams; she realizes the authority isn't investigating the phenomenon, it's managing it. She escapes with a stolen data slate showing the hold's true contents: people. Emotional beat: righteous fury and the cost of knowing.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Knocked
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. Ngozi, drawn by the dream's voice, finds Felix's ship and tells him the counting in her dream matches the hold's life-support cycle. Felix denies it, but his hands shake. Emotional beat: denial cracking against a child's terrible certainty.

chapters.title: Purge Order
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The authority issues a sanitation order for Felix's ship, scheduled within thirty hours. He realizes the backups will be erased and the children's dreams blamed on a contaminant. He must choose: run clean, or run guilty. Emotional beat: the moment complicity ends.

chapters.title: Stealing What Is Already His
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada, Felix, and Ngozi board the ship as authority crews arrive. A tense, near-bloodless theft: Ada fakes a quarantine breach, Felix flies them out on a cargo drone's transponder. Emotional beat: exhilaration laced with the knowledge there is no going back.

chapters.title: Voices in the Wiring
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In open space, Felix finally opens the hold. The backups stir when he speaks, and one of them—his own face, five years younger—answers through the ship's comm. Emotional beat: horror giving way to an unbearable intimacy with himself.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada explains the plan: the dead-space relay can broadcast the backups' testimony to every colony at once, but reaching it means crossing contested orbits where both the authority and scavver fleets hunt them. Emotional beat: fragile hope with a map of dangers.

chapters.title: Ngozi's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. The backups need a living mind to anchor their broadcast, and the children's shared dream makes Ngozi the only candidate. She agrees before the adults finish arguing. Emotional beat: a child claiming agency the adults wanted to deny her.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A scavver fleet corners the ship; Felix negotiates passage by offering navigation data, buying hours and an enemy. The authority's pursuit ship shadows them at the system's edge. Emotional beat: the cost of allies who are only allies until they aren't.

chapters.title: The Backup's Confession
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The younger Felix-copy reveals why Felix fled New Lagos five years ago: he signed the transport order that filled the hold, then erased his own memory of it. Emotional beat: identity as a thing that can be edited, and the shame that survives editing.

chapters.title: Ada's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada finds her own sister among the backups, harvested after the 'accident' that ended Ada's career. She nearly jettisons the hold to spare herself the grief. Emotional beat: justice and vengeance pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Signal Race
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. The authority begins jamming the relay corridor; the children on the colony fall into deeper, dangerous dreams as the network strains. Ngozi realizes the backups are dying by degrees. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They cross into dead space where no law, signal, or rescue exists. The ship grows strange—dreams bleed into the corridors, and Felix speaks with his copy for hours. Emotional beat: liminal calm before the storm, two selves circling forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Scavver's Price
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The scavver fleet returns to collect more than data, demanding the ship itself. Ada trades her medical skills and the truth of what's in the hold, turning scavvers into unlikely witnesses. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, improvised and costly.

chapters.title: Relay Station Zero
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They reach the ancient relay, derelict but alive, humming with the same counting voice from the children's dream. Authority warships enter the system behind them. Emotional beat: awe and the closing of a trap.

chapters.title: What Ngozi Saw in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. Anchoring the broadcast, Ngozi experiences the backups' memories whole—the harvests, the erasures, Felix's signature. She must decide whether to show the colonies everything, including Felix's guilt. Emotional beat: a child weighing mercy against truth.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The authority demands surrender as the broadcast begins. Felix merges a fragment of his mind with the network so the testimony can speak in a living voice—surrendering the self he was. Emotional beat: climax; sacrifice as the only honest testimony.

chapters.title: The Falling of the Authority
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Across the colonies, the signal lands. Dockworkers walk out, assessors defect, the authority's own ships refuse orders. Ada treats the first wounded of the collapse and finally grieves her sister. Emotional beat: catharsis, justice arriving messy and real.

chapters.title: Which of Us Came Home
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix returns to New Lagos, no longer sure which memories are his, and finds the children waiting—Ngozi among them—having chosen to remember him whole, guilt included. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt not as certainty but as being witnessed.

chapters.title: Rising, Again
chapters.summary: Ngozi's POV. Months later, the colony rebuilds; the backups wake in shifts, and the relay hums with open testimony. Ngozi, no longer dreaming alone, writes the first line of the colony's new record. Emotional beat: resolution—power watched, identity shared, justice institutionalized at last.
